ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening is required at formation and every material event: name-match all UBOs, directors, managers, and authorized signatories against the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals List, OFAC Consolidated Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, PRC Ministry of Public Security counter-terrorism and money-laundering lists, MOFCOM unreliable-entity list, and Taiwan designated sanctions/PEP databases. Determine whether any shareholder or controller is a domestic or foreign politically exposed person (PEP), including immediate family members and close associates. Run enhanced due diligence on PEPs and high-risk jurisdictions with source-of-wealth and source-of-funds evidence, independent UBO verification, and risk-rating forms. Apply the 25-percent ownership threshold for UBO identification and require senior-management approval for any red flags.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: SAMR Enterprise Name Self-Service Declaration and Reservation Portal within the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System (NECIPS)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: In mainland China, an enterprise name must be in simplified Chinese. The statutory four-tier composition is administrative division + distinctive name + line of business/industry + organizational form (limited liability company). A foreign investor's name must be transliterated into Chinese using standard character tables; pinyin is used only for filing systems, not the registered name. Traditional Chinese characters from Taiwanese documents must be converted to simplified Chinese in the registration filing. English-only names and Roman letters are generally prohibited except for certain internationally recognized acronyms approved by SAMR.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration with the same local SAMR bureau within 15 days from receipt, attaching the rejection notice, the reservation application number, amended Articles of Association, and a side-by-side comparison showing compliance with the four-tier naming formula. The SAMR bureau must issue a written decision; if it upholds the rejection, the applicant may commence an administrative lawsuit in the competent local people's court within six months. A reserved name may be extended once for a further 30 days before expiry by filing an extension request through the name-reservation portal, provided the underlying registration application remains pending.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a WFOE engaged in data center colocation leasing. The local SAMR, tax bureau, and banks mandatorily require a physical business address; the entity must have a lease or property ownership document. A virtual office is rejected for tax registration and bank account opening because the industry requires demonstrable technical facilities, on-site staff, power supply, and server equipment, and the tax authority will cross-check utility usage and site access. The registered address must match the actual operational site for colocation leasing; any divergence triggers suspension of electronic tax invoice issuance and bank settlement rights.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease agreement and property ownership evidence; (2) company plaque and visible signage; (3) on-site staffing; (4) server racks, cabling, UPS, and cooling systems; (5) electricity and bandwidth contracts; (6) fire-safety and data-security compliance. Quantified risk: 70 percent inspection likelihood for data-center lessors during the first 18 months; 90 percent if the registered office is a virtual mailbox or lacks physical infrastructure. Registries conduct unannounced inspections on average one to two times per year in this sector.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Act of the Republic of China (Taiwan), as amended; specifically Articles 98 to 113 on limited companies, Article 100 on capital, Article 129 on mandatory provisions in the Articles of Incorporation, Articles 156 and 161 on share capital and share certificates, and Articles 171 to 208 on shareholders meetings and directors, together with the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and its Enforcement Rules for the wholly foreign-owned enterprise approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Department of Commerce, Company Registration and Administration System (CRAS); Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment pre-approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application Form and the Articles of Incorporation, supported by the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, filed through the MOEA Company Registration and Administration System.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Taiwan Company Act does not impose a statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private limited company, and no blocked escrow account is required. The registered capital must nevertheless be fully paid by remittance into a Taiwan bank account established in the company's name, and a certified public accountant must issue a capital verification report evidencing receipt before the incorporation filing is accepted. The foreign investor must also comply with the approved investment amount stated in the Foreign Investment Approval Certificate.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] LIMITED COMPANY. At a meeting of the sole director of [COMPANY NAME] Limited Company (the Company) duly held on [DATE] at [TIME] at the registered office of the Company, the following resolutions were proposed, seconded, considered, and unanimously adopted, and the director declared that the resolutions were carried. 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND CONFIRMATION OF SHARE CAPITAL. RESOLVED that the initial registered share capital of the Company be fixed at [TWD AMOUNT], divided into [NUMBER] ordinary shares of par value [TWD AMOUNT] each, and that the sole shareholder has lawfully subscribed all such shares and fully paid the aggregate subscription price into the Company's bank account by wire transfer in accordance with the Foreign Investment Approval. FURTHER RESOLVED that the director be and is hereby authorised to prepare and execute share certificates, maintain the statutory shareholders register, and appoint a certified public accountant to verify the paid-in capital for filing with the Ministry of Economic Affairs. 2. REGISTERED OFFICE. RESOLVED that the registered office and statutory seat of the Company be and is hereby fixed at [FULL ADDRESS] in Taiwan, that such address shall be used for all service of process and statutory correspondence, and that the director be authorised to sign the lease, obtain the owner's consent letter, and file the address with the registrar. 3. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the Company is authorised to open operating accounts with [BANK NAME] and any other financial institutions, and that [NAME], as General Manager, and [NAME], as Director, be and are hereby appointed as authorised signatories, with mandate authority as will be specified on the bank signatory card, to sign all account documents, cheques, electronic payment instructions, foreign exchange contracts, and wire transfer requests, including ACH and SWIFT payment rails. 4. APPOINTMENT OF STATUTORY OFFICERS. RESOLVED that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as Director and Chairperson of the Board, and that [NAME] be and is hereby appointed as General Manager and Chief Executive Officer of the Company. The General Manager is vested with full authority, subject to applicable law and any limitations imposed by the Board, to manage the day-to-day business, hire and terminate employees, execute colocation and bare-metal server hosting contracts in the ordinary course of business, and represent the Company before government authorities, including the tax administration and environmental authorities. 5. RATIFICATION AND FILING AUTHORIZATION. RESOLVED that the Chairperson, General Manager, and any Company Secretary be and each is hereby authorised to prepare, execute, file, and prosecute the incorporation application, business registration, tax registration, labor insurance registration, and all ancillary documents required by law, and that all actions taken by the sole shareholder and the director before the date of this Resolution in furtherance of the Company's incorporation are hereby ratified, confirmed, and adopted as the acts of the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Foreign Investment Approval and Investment Commission Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Invest Taiwan One-Stop Service and online Foreign Investment Approval System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and submit the standard Foreign Investment Application together with notarized identity and corporate documents of the foreign shareholder, audited financial statements or a bank reference letter, a lawful-source-of-capital statement, a detailed business plan describing the Taiwan wholly foreign-owned enterprise for ISIC 6209 data center colocation leasing, the proposed registered capital, and the projected remittance schedule. The Investment Commission conducts a negative-list check under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals and verifies that no restricted industry is involved. Upon approval, the Commission issues a formal Foreign Investment Approval Certificate, which is a prerequisite to incorporation filing. Any change in the investment amount or shareholding after approval must be reported and re-approved before registration.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Application Form (Form A) signed by the applicant
Certificate of incorporation or business registration certificate of the foreign investing entity, notarized and with official traditional Chinese translation
Audited financial statements or a bank reference letter of the foreign investor
Power of attorney appointing the Taiwan resident representative and company formation agent, notarized if executed abroad
Passport or identification card copy of the investor's authorized signatory and the Taiwan local representative
Detailed business plan including ISIC 6209 data center colocation and bare-metal server hosting scope, capital plan, projected employment, and equipment list
Proposed Chinese and English company names and draft Articles of Incorporation
Source-of-funds statement and remittance schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Investment Commission issues a query, respond in writing within fourteen calendar days with corrected documents or traditional Chinese translations, and request a prompt re-review. If the application is suspended or refused, the applicant may file a petition for administrative appeal with the Ministry of Economic Affairs within thirty days, and thereafter an administrative lawsuit with the Taipei High Administrative Court, provided the defects are first cured. A timely letter of clarification will stop the procedural clock and avoid automatic rejection.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Reservation and Business Scope Pre-Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration and Administration System (CRAS) online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the MOEA Company Registration and Administration System and submit a name reservation application for the proposed Chinese legal name and corresponding English name. The system automatically checks national uniqueness and statutory name prohibitions, and confirms whether the proposed business scope covering data center colocation leasing and bare-metal server hosting can be lawfully included in the Articles of Incorporation. The name reservation is valid for six months and may be renewed. If the system flags a confusing similarity, the applicant must immediately submit at least two alternative names. The business scope should use the official Taiwan industry code corresponding to ISIC 6209 and avoid reserved or regulated wording such as banking or telecommunications.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Foreign Investment Approval certificate
Proposed Articles of Incorporation with exact business scope wording
Power of attorney of the formation agent
Identification document of the proposed responsible person
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of rejection due to name conflict, immediately file a revised name reservation with alternative proposed names. If the rejection is based on prohibited business scope, remove or revise the non-permissible wording and resubmit. The applicant may also file an administrative appeal to the Department of Commerce within thirty days, but the faster remedy is to amend the application online and reselect a distinct name.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Articles of Incorporation, Capital Payment, and CPA Capital Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Certified Public Accountant (CPA) appointed by the promoters; notarization if required; final filing authority is the MOEA Department of Commerce in a later incorporation filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The sole shareholder adopts written consent approving the Articles of Incorporation and nominates the first director and general manager. The Articles must conform to Company Act Article 129 and contain the company name, business scope, total issued capital, par value or number of shares, registered office, director provisions, and liquidation clauses. The shareholder then remits the entire subscription amount to a newly opened capital deposit account or the company's pre-registration bank account. The appointed CPA reviews the remittance evidence and Foreign Investment Approval and executes the capital verification report. The capital must be fully paid before the incorporation application is submitted; no escrow account is required, but the bank remittance certificate must match the approved foreign investment amount.
required_dossiers: Written resolution or minutes of the sole shareholder approving the Articles
Final text of the Articles of Incorporation
Bank remittance certificate and source-of-funds receipt
CPA capital verification report or accountant's report
Foreign Investment Approval certificate
Lease agreement for registered office and owner's written consent
Passport or identification card of the proposed director and general manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CPA queries the remittance or currency conversion, provide corrected bank statements and a reconciliation schedule. If the Foreign Investment Approval does not match the subscribed amount, apply to the Investment Commission for a post-establishment modification before filing. If the registered office consent is inadequate, replace the address and execute a new lease and owner consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Filing and Issuance of Incorporation Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration and Administration System (CRAS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed company incorporation application through CRAS attaching the Articles of Incorporation, shareholder resolution, capital verification report, Foreign Investment Approval certificate, registered office lease and consent, director consent, and identification documents. The company registration examiner verifies legal compliance with the Company Act, particularly paid-in capital, legality of the business scope, and name uniqueness. If satisfactory, the Department of Commerce registers the company and issues an electronic or paper Certificate of Incorporation. The company's existence, legal personality, and limitation of liability begin from this registration date. After receipt, execute the company seal, obtain a tax registration number, and open permanent bank accounts before commencing operations.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Application Form
Articles of Incorporation signed by the shareholder
Capital verification report by licensed CPA
Foreign Investment Approval certificate
Written consent of director and general manager
Registered office lease and owner's consent
Name reservation certificate
Filing fee payment receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a correction notice, cure the specific defect within fifteen calendar days and resubmit the corrected page. If the registrar refuses registration for an alleged legal defect, the applicant may file a written appeal with the Department of Commerce within thirty days. For minor data entry errors, request an administrative correction rather than a full new filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business, Tax, Labor, and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipality for profit-seeking enterprise business registration; National Taxation Bureau of the Ministry of Finance; Bureau of Labor Insurance; National Health Insurance Administration; local branch of the Ministry of Environment for facility filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the profit-seeking enterprise business registration with the local municipal government and the unified tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau within the statutory deadline, generally fifteen days after incorporation. Register as an employer with the Bureau of Labor Insurance and the National Health Insurance Administration and report all employees, including the resident manager. Apply for a Uniform Invoice Certificate if the company will issue electronic invoices for colocation rental and hosting fees. Open a payroll bank account and register the VAT withholding profile. If the data center owns standby diesel generators or stores hazardous materials, register the fixed stationary source or temporary storage area with the local environmental protection authority.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Application Form
Certificate of Incorporation
Foreign Investment Approval letter
National identification card or ARC of responsible person and local manager
Registered office lease and building use consent
Employment contracts and labor insurance payroll list
Uniform Invoice equipment registration form
Facility environmental self-reporting form if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If tax registration is delayed by a missing document, submit the outstanding item with a written explanation and request expedited handling; late registration penalties may be waived if the delay is attributable to the authority. If the local municipality refuses business registration for use certificate defects, obtain a temporary business use permit or relocate to a compliant building and refile.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Building Occupancy, Fire Safety, and Pre-Commissioning Facility Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Urban Development Bureau or Public Works Department; National Fire Agency of the Ministry of the Interior; Ministry of Environment; Ministry of Labor occupational safety administration; local electricity inspection authority
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the data center colocation hall accepts its first customer, obtain a building use permit or a change-of-use approval evidencing that the premises are classified for computer data center use and meet structural load requirements. Engage a registered fire safety equipment firm to install and certify fire alarms, extinguishers, emergency lighting, and, where required, an automatic fire suppression system; this certificate must be filed with the local fire department. Have a licensed structural and electrical engineer inspect the floor loading, UPS, generators, and main switchgear. If installed diesel generators meet stationary-source thresholds, obtain an air pollution permit or complete a self-registration. The fire safety management plan must name trained fire safety managers for each shift.
required_dossiers: Certificate of building completion or building occupancy license
Change-of-use approval for computer data center use
Structural floor-loading certificate by a licensed engineer
Fire safety equipment installation and inspection certificate
Fire safety management plan and fire safety manager appointment register
Electrical inspection report and generator emission calculations
Site plan and emergency escape route drawings
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the building inspector or fire department issues a non-compliance notice, implement the corrective action list within thirty days and request a re-inspection. If structural load is insufficient, reduce rack density and provide engineer-stamped load calculations. If generator emissions exceed permit thresholds, use cleaner fuel, add exhaust treatment, or redesign the emergency power architecture and resubmit the permit application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) for business registration; local Municipal Urban Development Bureau for building use; local Fire Department under the National Fire Agency for fire safety clearances; Ministry of Environment for air, wastewater, and hazardous waste permits; Ministry of Labor for occupational safety
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No dedicated data-center statutory operating license is issued in Taiwan, and the target business under ISIC 6209 data center colocation leasing does not require a special vertical concession. The facility must hold a general Business Registration Certificate and a Building Use Permit in the computer-processing use class, together with the facility-level fire and environmental permits described below.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (formerly Environmental Protection Administration), Executive Yuan, Taiwan
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Data center colocation is not listed as a Category A full-EIA facility in the Environmental Impact Assessment Act schedule. Unless the site is in an environmentally sensitive area or the total floor area and energy demand are large enough to trigger a project screening, the facility is generally exempt from a full EIA. At minimum, an Environmental Registration and self-reporting duty under the Air Pollution Control Act will apply if standby diesel generators are classified as stationary pollution sources; a full EIA may be directed by the competent authority for sensitive watershed or cultural heritage locations.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Quantitative compliance limits applicable to a data center operation in Taiwan include: wastewater discharge must meet Taiwan effluent standards, generally pH 6-9, suspended solids 30 mg/L or less, BOD5 30 mg/L or less, COD 100 mg/L or less, and discharge temperature 38 degrees Celsius or lower; cooling tower blowdown water must be treated for inhibitors and total residual chlorine below 0.02 mg/L. Diesel generators must use low-sulfur fuel and comply with stationary-source emission limits under the Air Pollution Control Act, including opacity not exceeding 10% and fuel sulfur content no more than 10 ppm; volatile organic compound emissions from any fuel or solvent storage must be controlled by sealed tanks and carbon or thermal oxidizer systems if required. Hazardous wastes such as spent lead-acid batteries, contaminated oil filters, used oil, and chemical absorbents must be stored in impervious secondary containment and removed by licensed waste carriers using the Ministry of Environment online manifest system within 90 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The operator must obtain a Fire Safety Certification under the Fire Services Act, including the fire safety equipment certificate and annual fire safety management plan filed with the local fire department. The building must pass a structural load inspection and receive a Building Use Permit for the data center occupancy class. Workplace safety approval is required under the Occupational Safety and Health Act: electrical installations must be inspected by a licensed electrical contractor, battery rooms must be ventilated with hydrogen detection and eye-wash stations, emergency exits and alarms must be tested, and a workplace accident insurance policy must be in force. If the building is required to provide civil defense shelter space under Taiwanese building regulations, the operator must preserve that designated space and include it in the emergency response plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance (MOF) of Taiwan, exercised through the regional National Taxation Bureaus; the online registration and electronic filing portal is the MOF Tax Entry Portal (etax.nat.gov.tw), supported by the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform for indirect tax administration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise formed as a Taiwan limited company, the foreign investor must first obtain investment approval from the Investment Commission of the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Foreign Investment Act, then complete company incorporation and business registration with the Ministry of Economic Affairs under the Company Act. Following approval, the company must apply to the regional National Taxation Bureau for Business Tax and profit-seeking enterprise tax registration to obtain the statutory Unified Business Number, which serves as the tax identification number for VAT, corporate income tax, electronic invoices, customs declarations, and employment matters. The application package includes the investment permit, articles of incorporation, company registration certificate, legal representative identification, business premises lease or ownership evidence, bank account proof, and a signed authorization for tax affairs. A foreign non-resident enterprise without a Taiwan establishment is not granted a Unified Business Number; instead, Taiwan-source payments are handled through withholding, and the non-resident may receive a temporary tax identity for filing purposes where required.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: the WFOE Ltd is treated as a Taiwan-resident profit-seeking enterprise subject to corporate income tax on its taxable profits; it is not a pass-through entity and has no statutory pass-through election.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Taiwan law does not provide a check-the-box entity classification election or a hybrid mismatch election for a WFOE Ltd; the entity must file as a profit-seeking enterprise under the Income Tax Act.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / Business Tax under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold applies to incorporated entities: every business engaged in taxable activity in Taiwan must complete Business Tax registration before commencing operations. Small-scale businesses with average monthly taxable turnover not exceeding NT$200,000 may qualify for a special presumptive business tax regime, but a data-center colocation and bare-metal server hosting WFOE is required to be fully VAT-registered.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The business must issue a statutory Uniform Invoice for every taxable sale. Under the Electronic Uniform Invoice regime, VAT-registered businesses use the MOF e-Invoice Integration Service Platform, connecting through a certified Turnkey service provider or a value-added e-invoice service provider. E-invoices must carry the serialized statutory Uniform Invoice number, include the buyer’s Unified Business Number where required, be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance platform for fiscal control and audit access, and be available for real-time inquiry by the National Taxation Bureau. There is no physical fiscal stamp, but digital transmission and preservation of the e-invoice records are mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated Business Tax applies to goods exported from Taiwan where the goods leave Taiwan customs territory under a valid customs export declaration and the export proceeds are repatriated in foreign exchange. Zero-rating also applies to services supplied to foreign enterprises without a Taiwan fixed place of business, or to foreign individuals, where the services are used or consumed outside Taiwan and the consideration is received in foreign exchange. For data-center colocation and bare-metal server hosting, physical rack space, power, and cooling located in Taiwan are deemed consumed in Taiwan and remain taxable at 5%; zero-rating is available only for separately documented qualifying offshore services such as remote management of servers located outside Taiwan or subscription services delivered and consumed entirely outside Taiwan, provided the foreign-exchange and service-usage evidence is substantiated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export customs report issued by Taiwan Customs)
Ocean or air Bill of Lading / Airway Bill evidencing export movement
Commercial invoice for the exported goods or offshore services
Bank foreign-exchange settlement certificate / Inward Remittance Advice evidencing repatriation of export proceeds
Certificate of origin or export permit where applicable
Service contract or performance evidence substantiating offshore use for zero-rated services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The National Taxation Bureau and Taiwan Customs may audit the complete documentary chain, including customs declarations, transport documents, invoices, contracts, and bank foreign-exchange records. If a zero-rating claim is not substantiated within the statutory deadline or the export proceeds are not repatriated within 180 days without an approved extension, the tax authority will reassess the Business Tax at 5% on the unsubstantiated receipts, impose delinquency interest, and may levy administrative fines under the Value-added and Non-value-added Business Tax Act. In cases of fraudulent invoices, fictitious export declarations, or deliberate evasion, the responsible person may be subject to criminal prosecution under the Tax Evasion and Punishment Act, and retrospective clawbacks for prior periods will be assessed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBoC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE), the latter being the statutory foreign exchange administration under the PBoC's authority
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Current account convertibility is effectively granted to trade-in-services flows: data center colocation and bare-metal hosting fees received from Taiwan and other non-resident clients qualify as computer and information services income and may be settled through a domestic Foreign Exchange Settlement Account upon submission of the service contract, commercial invoice, proof of service delivery, and tax payment certificates. Capital account items remain restricted: FDI equity injections into the WFOE require prior Foreign Investment Information Registration and SAFE verification through the designated bank, with funds confined to the registered business scope and the negative list discipline; use of capital proceeds for equity investment, entrusted lending, or non-operating expenditures is prohibited. Profit remittance to the Taiwan shareholder is permissible after the annual audit, full corporate income tax settlement, and completion of the SAFE Foreign Exchange Remittance Application, which is processed on a true-and-legal basis. The New Taiwan Dollar (TWD) is not a convertible onshore settlement currency in mainland China; cross-strait receipts are therefore routed through USD or RMB via the Cross-Strait RMB clearing mechanism. Overall, the regime is best characterized as full current-account convertibility with post-event verification, and controlled capital-account convertibility with bank-mediated administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio applies. China abolished compulsory foreign exchange surrender for export proceeds in 2012. For the WFOE's service exports (ISIC 6209 colocation receivables), foreign currency proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic designated settlement account and reported through the international balance-of-payments statistical regime (涉外收支申报) within five banking days of credit. Funds may be retained indefinitely in foreign currency, converted at market rate at the exporter's discretion, or applied directly to current account disbursements. No minimum percentage is mandated for conversion into RMB. Cross-strait Taiwan-origin proceeds are additionally captured under the cross-strait trade settlement statistical framework but are not subject to surrender ratios.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Settlement Account plus current-account RMB/Foreign Exchange Settlement Account; designated Cross-Strait RMB clearing agent

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rated Low-Medium. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Airwallex, Currenxie, PingPong, and WorldFirst are not licensed deposit-taking institutions in mainland China and cannot open domestic RMB settlement accounts, cannot receive FDI capital injection proceeds, and cannot discharge the WFOE's SAFE reporting obligations. Their practical role is limited to offshore collection of Taiwan and global colocation client fees in USD, HKD, or CNH, followed by remittance to the WFOE's domestic bank account via MT103. Legal constraints include the requirement that cross-border payment institutions hold a PBoC Payment License or operate under the NRA/OSA framework; for B2B service receipts of a regulated nature, over-reliance on an unlicensed EMI is inadvisable from an audit-integrity and tax-verification perspective. The recommended architecture is a domestic bank primary account with an offshore EMI used only as a sub-collection rail for small recurring fees.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is required. Under the PBoC Customer Due Diligence Rules (中国人民银行令〔2018〕第1号) and SAFE practice directives, the legal representative, authorized signatories, and ultimate beneficial owners must attend an in-person KYC interview at the branch compliance desk during initial onboarding. Remote video onboarding is available only in limited pilots and only for holders of PRC identity certificates. Directors or shareholders resident in Taiwan must provide corporate and identity documents authenticated by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF, 海基會) and verified through the Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Straits (ARATS, 海协会); alternatively, a notarized power of attorney executed before a Taiwan notary is acceptable, with the mainland bank conducting biometric verification of the appointed local representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity created by a cross-strait multi-layer holding structure (Taiwan parent above mainland WFOE)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full UBO chain chart identifying all natural persons with 25% or greater control; certified Taiwan company registry extract and shareholders' register; SEF-ARATS authenticated corporate documents; statutory declaration as to source of funds; two years of audited financial statements; notarized power of attorney; and a written group-structure explanation letter approved by the compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment pattern mismatch where large upfront or lump-sum colocation fees arrive from newly registered counterparties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Master Service Agreement specifying rack space, power capacity (kW), network ports, and service levels; itemized billing schedule; data center facility lease agreement proving the WFOE's physical operations; DCIM and metering logs evidencing service consumption; tenant KYC files for each colocation client; and matched tax filing and invoice records.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-value outbound disbursements to Taiwan infrastructure or bandwidth providers lacking a physical contract trail
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed Service Level Agreements with Taiwan vendors; commercial invoices; delivery evidence in the form of network uptime reports, maintenance logs, and hardware transit records; cross-strait customs or logistics documentation where equipment crosses the border; and bank reference letters from the counterparty's financial institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Adverse media, PEP, or sanctions-screening hit against a minority shareholder or indirect director
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-declaration form; comprehensive adverse-media search report; negative-news explanation memorandum; corporate board resolution confirming the investment rationale; biographical and source-of-wealth statement; and a remediation letter signed by both the compliance officer and the affected individual.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant FDI routing sequence: (i) the Taiwan shareholder executes the equity subscription agreement and the WFOE completes the Foreign Investment Information Report with the market regulatory authority and the SAFE Foreign Investment Registration through the settlement bank; (ii) the WFOE opens a SAFE-designated Capital Account (资本金账户) at a tier-1 Chinese commercial bank; (iii) the inward remittance is transmitted via SWIFT MT103 from the Taiwan shareholder's bank, using SAFE BOP declaration code 621011 (外国来华直接投资——投资资本金, Foreign Direct Investment capital injection). The receiving bank authenticates the underlying, verifies the registration quota, credits the Capital Account, and enters the transaction into the SAFE Foreign Exchange Administration System. In pilot free-trade zones, the capital-income payment convenience policy enables direct payment of wages, rent, utilities, and taxes without per-transaction prior approval, subject to a 30-day post-event documentary review. Any increase in registered capital requires an amended information report and registration update before the additional remittance is accepted.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound clearing rails are segmented by purpose: (a) cross-border service fees to Taiwan or global vendors (bandwidth, maintenance, software licenses, remote hands) are settled by SWIFT MT103 from the WFOE's current-account settlement book, accompanied by a trade-in-services declaration, VAT withholding, and corporate income tax withholding certification; (b) capital equipment imports (servers, network hardware, cooling infrastructure) are executed through Commercial Letters of Credit — sight LCs or usance LCs issued by the WFOE's bank with documents-against-payment terms, matched to customs declarations under equipment import codes; (c) intra-group treasury flows across the Taiwan Strait may be routed through the Cross-Strait RMB clearing mechanism, with Bank of China (Taipei) acting as the Taiwan clearing bank and PBoC as the onshore clearing authority, enabling CNH settlement without the USD correspondent chain; and (d) domestic operating liquidity (utilities, payroll, colocation landlord rent) is cleared through CNAPS and the ACS high-value payment system using the RMB basic deposit account.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore plain-vanilla FX forwards (远期结售汇) with real trade background documentation for USD/RMB colocation receivables
Onshore FX swaps (外汇掉期) for short-term USD/RMB working-capital conversion
Plain-vanilla FX options and option combination structures authorized under SAFE's FX Options pilot, requiring a verified current-account underlying
Offshore CNH non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on RMB/TWD exposure executed through a licensed offshore bank or Taiwan OBU; onshore NDFs are not permitted
Cross-currency swaps (双币种掉期) for medium-term USD-denominated FDI shareholder loans, subject to SAFE debt registration and external-debt quota compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Report of Responsible Persons and Major Shareholders (Company Act Article 22-1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company Responsible Persons and Major Shareholders Online Reporting Platform
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before 31 March for data as of preceding 31 December; any change reported within 15 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of NT$50,000 to NT$500,000; successive fines until filing; persistent refusal may block corporate registration changes and lead to MOEA order of dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Operating Status Report of Mainland-Funded Investment Enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 June following fiscal year end (calendar fiscal year unless approval obtained for a different period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Investment Commission administrative penalties; suspension of inward/outward capital remittance, profit repatriation, share transfer or investment applications; repeated non-compliance may result in withdrawal of investment approval

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return and Unappropriated Earnings Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 May following the tax year for a 31 December fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of self-assessed tax if filed after deadline but before tax investigation; additional penalty up to NT$30,000; daily interest on unpaid tax; continued non-payment may trigger tax lien, enforcement, and court-ordered dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Approval of Business Report, Financial Statements, and Profit Appropriation or Loss Set-off Proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company minute book and statutory records at the registered office; filed with MOEA only when the resolution amends articles or directorship details
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies); written consent may substitute for a formal AGM in closely held companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Violation of Company Act meeting rules can result in fines against responsible persons and MOEA order requiring convening or correction; failure to approve financial statements may also affect profit distribution and shareholder inspection rights

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory CPA audit applies under Company Act Article 20 and MOEA threshold where paid-in capital reaches NT$30,000,000 or where MOEA specifically requires a certified audit; public issuers are always audited. Data-center colocation leasing does not create a separate statutory audit trigger.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Non-public companies apply ROC Business Entity Accounting Standards (EAS); public companies and those electing to do so apply Taiwan-IFRS; taxable income is reconciled under the Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Assessment Rules. Commercial Accounting Act requires accounting ledgers and financial statements to be preserved for at least 10 years and supporting vouchers for at least 5 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan requires an annual electronic confirmation under Company Act Article 22-1 covering directors, supervisors, managers and all shareholders holding more than 1% of issued shares; the report is required even when there is no shareholding change. Any shareholding transfer affecting foreign or mainland-China investor status must also be reported to the Investment Commission and reflected in the statutory registers within 15 days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book of Shareholders and Directors
Accounting ledgers and financial statements prepared under the Commercial Accounting Act

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Flat 20% rate with first NT$120,000 exempt; 5% surtax on undistributed earnings; R&D credit up to 20% and Smart Machinery/5G investment credits (3–5%) under the Industry Innovation Act; AMT 12%
